title: DC Vance Joseph, STC/Asst. HC Darren Rizzi and OC Davis Webb meet the media ahead of Week 9
text: Coach, what have you seen in the uh development of Bryce Emmy? You saw him a couple years ago and just where he's at right now? >> Well, he's very smart. He's very accurate. Um he's he's played good football. Um last couple weeks he's got some pressure, you know, that's affected him a little bit, but it's going to be a challenge to get him stopped. It's a it's a good offense. They have really good skilled players at the receiver spot and the halfback spot and tight end spot. So, it's going to be a challenge. You know, it's it's it's an NFL game that being our best is uh important. >> Two weeks in a row, we've seen the defense kind of end the game, goal line stand. What does it say about your unit to buckle down as tight as they did there two consecutive weeks? >> I think we just play, you know, we don't worry about, you know, where the ball's put down. We just play. Um those things we practice every single week. You know, I'm not surprised that we're good down there. You know, we spend a bunch of time down there. It's been our fourth year together. We have our four or five calls we love down there that we're good at, you know, and so if we do it right, we expect to win. >> A guy like JL who can hit, right? >> Sure. >> Um what what is what does he need to do to get more time at safety? >> Well, you know, he he is he's playing now. You know, he's he's waited his time, Mike. I mean, we have a lot of depth in the back end especially, and um you know, he's been itching to play for a long time. Trust me, he calls me all the time. So, um, you know, he got his chance to play on Sunday, uh, afternoon and he played well, you know, but that's what he's always done. You know, we've got a bunch of kids in the back end that when the numbers call, they play well. So, that's a good thing for a coach and a and a team to have great depth like that. >> In terms you guys need the NFL on defensive snaps. Sean said he was concerned about that on Monday. I'm curious from your perspective, what does that do to your defense? Are you worried about the amount of snaps you're flying? >> No, no, we don't worry about that. We have a fairly young defense and again we have great depth you know so we have guys who can fill in and play you know even during the game we can you know we can split reps so our concern is always playing good football you know if it takes 50 takes 70 snap we're going to play those snaps to go win the game so you know we have never talked about that ever in our room >> Alex Alex is another year removed from that ACL injury and he's talked about how much better he's felt. Have you seen that on tape? Just the the elevated level. >> Well, I saw it I saw it last year. I mean, he's guys, he's played good football for us for a long time. And it's a shame that he's finally being recognized for it, you know, but I've known he's he's a pretty good player for a long time. I watch film every day and I told him this last year. I don't see a lot of guys better than you, you know, and obviously the green dot for us is very important. So, outside of him making a bunch of plays, man, I mean, he's our quarterback on defense. So for me, he's been the best backer in football for a long time. >> I'm not surprised. >> You surprised that it hasn't been recognized before that? >> No, that's that's the league. That's the league, you know. And again, when you're playing good on defense, guys do get recognized, you know, and he's been consistent for a long time. He had 171 tackles what, two years ago, right? No one talks about that. So, >> I'm not surprised he's playing well again. >> Have you seen Malcolm Roach take a jump with some increased opportunity this year? Absolutely. That was that was a must for us, you know, and he's done that. You know, Malcolm's on every single day. He's got this unique quickness and and also he's stout, you know, for a quick guy. So, he can play nose, he can play four eye, he plays three technique, he's our interior rusher on third down. So, he's been a big part of what we've done here the last two years. >> It's guys like Seavon and Q who who you guys drafted last year, but largely kind of uh waited their turn last year. what what goes on when you have young players like that to make sure that going into year two they're they're >> ready well it's coaching you know it's coaching and I think when you're picking your roster you have to pick your roster you know with with guys that fit your your scheme you know I think here that's what we've done you know so when you lose one player we have guys who can fill in who's got the same skill set you know so I'm not surprised those kids play wall again it's NFL football it's the same coach it's the same room, you know, so when it's their turn to play, they play the standard, right? If they don't fit and they can't play, they shouldn't be here, right? So every guy on this team who makes our roster on defense, right, if they have to play for us, nothing changes in my mind, right? Let's go win the game. Now, it's certain areas I can't call certain things with certain players, but the standard in doing it right, that never changes here. having having Pastor Tan back last week and the future as [clears throat] well. How much does that change the game plan and maybe make it more simpler, easier game plan? >> Well, I don't I wouldn't say that. Our plan changes every week according to who we're playing. Pat obviously can take away the best receiver or one side of the field. Like last week's game, I don't think Patrick even looked his way but one time on RBO, you know. So Pat Pat played well last week. I mean, he tackled really well obviously on the goal line, but his coverage has been been outstanding from Sam Fran to last week. So, um, having good players is always a good thing and having the best court in football is a great thing. >> Coach, you mentioned JL calls you. I know you guys advocate for themselves, but how often over the years have you had guys call and ask for or come up to you and ask or kind of want that playing time? >> Most guys who are good players have done that, you know, who's become, you know, obviously starters. Jel Skinner, in my opinion, is a Pro Bowl teamer, you know? So, when guys play teams that well, playing defense is very similar, right? It's getting off blocks, it's being physical, it's being fast, taking great angles. Buddha Baker made his first Pro Bowl as a teamer, right? And he made his next six as a safety, you know, with no interceptions in the first three years. So, I'm not again not surprised that Devin Key can play for us, so we can still win, you know? Same with Skinner. You watch him practice every day. Again, it's the same coaching, the same scheme. So just doing it right, you know, being 111th is important in our room, but those kids, they all want a chance to play, you know, and when it happens and they have success, man, that's that's the program. That's the culture we build and run here. >> Uh whereas you heard BJ just talk about uh JL and Keith, but when I guess I'm asking this plenty, but when those guys are thrust into more action because Andrew's in front of them, how tricky is that? make your Sunday because you love to have them as much as you can, but you may not get them as much as you normally have them. >> Yeah, I mean that's I think that's probably the number one job of the of the special teams guys to manage a roster, right? And so uh first off, kudos to them um for being options to go play on defense. Again, no surprise. I heard VJ say it. Uh both those guys uh made plays, a bunch of plays for us on the special team side. They're both really good athletes. They cover a lot of ground. They have good range. Uh and they're high football IQ guys. So they're great guys to have on our team. Now the the challenge for me obviously is is you know where do we make up those reps. Um and that's you know that goes back to training everybody on the roster from day one back to OTAA is training camp and that's where all that work comes in. So you know we'll we'll come up with a plan and the best however it's going to work out we'll uh you know we'll manufacture the best 11 guys out there and get them ready to play. But I I like the depth of our roster. I think it's one of our strengths I think. Um and so whoever steps up next guy up will you know will fill in and do an adequate job. I'm sure of it. Well, and then how much is it kind of player dependent and or stakes dependent, if you will, so that depending on the time of the game, certain guys you'll still use on teams even if they're starting and playing 60 70 snaps on on the side of >> Yeah, I think one of the things people not realize is we we do a pretty good job of keeping track of reps during the game. You know, we have guys up in the box kind of doing rep count and making sure no one's getting, you know, too many. You know, as you know, there's some games where you might have 18 special teams plays and there's some games where you might have 35. It it really just depends how the game plays out. So, we'll do a good job. We'll have a plan kind of going in. Um, you know, dispel those guys if needed. Um, and you know, they're going to have to do obviously some things. They might not do the full uh workload as they normally do. And and then and then again, they might depending on how the game plays out. So, um you know, so we'll kind of track that as we go. And uh but yeah, my uh my depth chart sheet will be an interesting uh it'll be an interesting one. Be like the old uh what's the movie? The old Matrix. It'll be a lot of lot of lot of stuff going on there. So coach Andy Andy Reid indicated that that missed field goal from Bucker, he couldn't kick it straight or left because of the pressure coming down on that side. What did you see from from the pressure that that you're using? >> Yeah, I'm not sure what coach I didn't really hear Coach Greed's comments, but I will say this. I thought our field goal block unit uh has done a really good job this, you know, these first eight games. Uh really good effort. I did think if the ball was on target, we had a chance at it. You know, there's a few hands in the kind of in the kick lane, if you will. Um, you never know how, you know, with the elevation and all that, but I I'll tell you what, our effort, we did collapse in uh that side on that field goal and it looked like if he did hit it straight, man, we had an opportunity there. So, uh, really really proud of the effort and the execution by that by that group. Um, because that's really an effort unit. You know, there's a lot of units that are execution. A lot of units are X's and O's and scheme. Not that one. That's an effort unit. Your field goal block is kind of the unit you hang your hat on. Those guys got to give effort. had they had no chance because the ball's out of there, you know, in a second and a half. So, if you don't give effort off the ball, you got no chance there. So, great job by them. >> The the extra point at the end when it's raining like that, how much even on an extra point is it difficult to go up and and how do you work on kind of those situations for for being >> Yeah, it's I I you know, listen, I think obviously because we play outdoors, you know, at all our home games, we we you know, weekly we'll maybe do some wet ball drills and things like that. Um it's not really the it's weird when the K balls are a different ball than a quarterback ball. they're a little bit smoother because they get kind of warped. And so when those balls get a little bit wet, they actually get really slippery. It's not the ball that's soaked. It's the ball when it just starts raining that if you've talked to all the specialists over the years, the snappers and the holders and you know the punter catching the catching the operation, those are the ones. So right away when you see any precipitation come down, those guys off are off on the side and they're getting work and you know whether or not they use a towel, gloves, whatever we're allowed to use. Um but yeah, it it certainly makes an operation. So, as soon as we we know we're going to get any kind of weather, um you know, we certainly practice it and then those guys on game day, you know, um are going to be keep working on the sideline and and kind of, you know, gauge the weather. >> You appreciate that one a little bit more when it goes through. [laughter] >> No question. And even the punts, you know, the punt operation, you know, that 15 yard snap back there, uh same thing. And the snapper, you know, when he's down there holding the ball and it gets wet. So, there's a lot of there's a lot of things that go into it. Um so, you know, that's that's a big deal. It's a big deal when the when the weather comes around with the operation. So, we make, you know, we we make sure we work at it. >> You can obviously simulate a really wet ball, but do you do like get sprinklers out and and misty situations so that they feel the whole thing? >> Oh, yeah. We do a little bit of everything. So, I mean, you could take a dry ball and get like a water bottle. Yeah. >> Just kind of mist it. Um, you know, in the colder weather, we've we've had balls in the freezer before all day sitting in the freezer and bring those out because they obviously get, you know, the the PSIs, you know, and all that kind of get different and it kind of ball gets a little harder. So we we try to simulate all that, you know, all those sprinklers on >> all those situations >> guys during >> No, you know, we've had fun with it before, but but but no, the ball, it's really the ball and the plant foot that are the things you worry about the most, right? The football getting it back there and then when the kicker comes in at a good range or even the punter, that plant foot sometimes you got to really be controlled. So sometimes they'll kind of shorten it up a little bit depending on how wet wet it gets, whether it's rain or snow. So there's a lot of factors that go into it, but we we definitely practice. We practice the set the wet soggy ball and then the one that just gets a little bit out. >> There's a lot of the teams when they get excited come to Denver for the altitude kicking. Is there a challenge going down to sea level? Is there any challenge there? [snorts] >> Well, I I think the the pregame warm-up for us may be more important than any other position because you kind of get an idea of, you know, how the ball's going to travel on that particular day. you know, whether it's wind, weather, you know, listen, I I've coached at sea level for for 16 or more than 16 years NFL and then a bunch of years in college. Listen, the ball may not travel as well. Uh we'll see what the weather is there. But that's the pregame for the kicker and the punter are probably more important than than people would would anticipate because you kind of get the wind direction. You know, which way if it's a sideways wind or north south wind, if you will, um then how well the ball's traveled. So, we kind of have, you know, coach will always ask me right before kickoff kind of, hey, what's our line going each way, uh, for us and them and so, you know, um, the ball, you know, the ball certainly travels a little bit better here in altitude, but it it it I think sometimes it gets overblown and I over overdid a little bit. We'll see. We'll see how it is there in pregame on on Sunday morning. >> Davis, you feel like the offense has finally turned the corner in a major way compared to the first few weeks? >> I still think it's a race to improve. you know, as soon as I say that, we might be back to square one, you know, so we'll uh continue the streak we're on. It's a great winning streak, obviously, and we got a tough one in Charlotte coming up. >> When you see Bo, throw the waddle down the seam or the one down the left sideline to to Courtland, what does that say to you just in terms of how he's seeing the field or the confidence he has and let him rip there? >> I think he said he's seen it well. He's delivering it with conviction and uh he's got a good rhythm, you know, going. I think we said that before the Arizona game. go on a little run here and I think uh he's doing a good job really just settling in and trusting his teammates and allowing the ball to be pushed down field. >> What's it do for the offense when you got a rookie coming in like Jonah and you can see the juice of the spark that he that he provides when he has a ball? >> I think that started since rookie mini camp and then in the preseason game against Atlanta and then uh the Jacksonville game and now this game. I think every time he gets an opportunity he's showed up and his teammates love him. He's smart, he's mature and uh he's going to continue to get better which is awesome. Do you enjoy when we get on a streak like this after, you know, the play play calling for, you know, how that changed a little bit? Have you been able to kind of enjoy this run or you kind of like, well, I'd love to get another chance at this game, but it's working. You never you never break them? >> Uh, I'll get another chance. I I'm 31. Um, but I want to win and um that's the number one thing. I'm a team first guy. I always have been that way. Um, I've been benched as a player. Um, now I say as a coach basically. Uh, so I I think it is what it is. I I knew that was a chance coming into this job. Um, but I'm more excited about the what how many games have we won in a row? Four. Let's make it five. >> David, I think Bo was talking yesterday about how Sean kind of has the right message for the team each week depending on what you need. After an emotional win like that, just how you seen him kind of handle the team this week to get you guys ready for Carolina? I think if you look at Carolina's record, you could be one of those guys that overlooks them. But if you look at the Chicago game, they put up a lot of points on offense. You look at the Detroit game, they beat them. Uh there's plenty of examples of this team being really, really good. They're a playoff team last year. Arguably should have beat the Rams in the playoffs last year. Um so, you know, they're a couple plays away from having a winning record. So, um this is the NFL. There's not many cupcakes out there. So, this is going to be a good one on S Sunday. How much does the coaching staff use a by-week to to self scout as opposed to like also trying to get away and get a little break in this off season? >> I think everyone every staff's a little different, every philosophy is a little different. I like to do it at the beginning of the week and then kind of relax towards the end. Um, so we haven't been with Shawn yet about how we're going to go about that, but every Monday we kind of start our self scout process. We've done that a little bit more this year than years past. We just kind of updated a few things systemwise that makes it a little bit more efficient. Davis, how much extra work is there when they make a coordinator change or move on from a coordinator, you know, in the middle of the year, so you don't know exactly what you'll be getting with the new play call. >> Yeah, I think uh the first quarter is going to be interesting in regards of kind of seeing how what they have new, what's kind of the same. Uh a couple players that are banged up and are they going to play or they not? Obviously schematics. So I think the first quarter is going to be a really interesting quarter and then I think the game's going to settle down within that to the second to the fourth. So, you know, but you can say the same thing about Kansas City versus us. Um, obviously still Sean's offense, so there wasn't much change. Um, mid-season changing a bunch is probably going to be tough, but there'll definitely be some wrinkles and uh we're prepared to uh attack it.

title: Laken Tomlinson 1-on-1: Getting comfortable at RG
text: Looking at the right side, how did that second start in that position go last week? How do you feel about it?  So, how do you like it? The truth is, it's great. Especially having the opportunity to practice this week has been very good.   Is it not a big deal for you because you already know it, or do you have to change everything and it's not that big of a deal ?   I mean, it's definitely a challenge, especially last week. But this week, you know, especially coming up to the long weekend, I had extra time to go over things on my own, work on my technique, and just work on reversing things, you know, in terms of technique.  And having these two days of practice, I definitely feel much more comfortable now. Throughout your career you have been part of some truly fantastic ground games . What's happening with ours? What's your take on it?   He's coming, man.  You know, you just have to have faith and keep working hard.   You know, there's an old saying: keep working hard, man, and you know, keep feeling the ball, keep running with it and you'll see how it comes, I promise you. One last thing, how are you enjoying it so far? You know, joining the team mid- season and all that, but contributing right away, how does it feel to be here? Man, to be honest, I feel blessed. It's an amazing place, an amazing franchise.  Obviously, I heard a lot of great things about this place in Green Bay. It's incredible, and, you know, obviously, to run into familiar faces that I've crossed paths with over the years , and I'm just getting to know the locker room and the guys here.  It's been fantastic and I'm grateful for the opportunity I have here.

title: Andrew Janocko and Rob Leonard Presser - 11.5.26
text: I definitely would. I definitely would. But um I might get y'all out of home for that one. >> [laughter] >> Uh you guys have talked a lot about the first drive coming out of halftime. And uh this week it was it was successful. I guess what does it do for the team to just kind of build that confidence coming out of half and having that uh scoring drive? >> When you look at when you look at football games, anytime that you can score at the end of the half and score coming out of the half, that's a tremendous advantage. And that's just statistically and I think every team really preaches preaches that stuff uh preaches, you know, being able if you can double dip or get the score at the end of the half, getting a score at the beginning of half, but just changing or keeping momentum, that's always something that you're looking to do. >> Is specifically some when when there's something you guys talk about, I know, you know, Clint has talked about it, Kirk has talked about it to get that get that right, how rewarding is it to see it actually come into fruition? >> That's really something that as, you know, as the head coach sets a vision for something, it's on all of us as an organization to to get that done. So when when he sets a goal for the week or, you know, he sets something that that he's talked about, that he makes it a priority, it's something that that we you know, we take to heart and we put it implement it in practice, we implement it in things that, you know, we're trying to do, how we're going about how we're going about our business, our planning. And then when it, you know, when it comes to fruition, we're just, you know, we're really carrying out his vision and that that's you know, that's what it takes to be successful. >> How would you evaluate Trey's first career start? >> Think he's came out, competed, did a lot of good things, did a lot of things to build on. It was great that there are some things that he's that he'll learn from and grow and just being out there competing and helping us get a win was was huge huge for his confidence and huge for us going forwards in offense. >> What do you make of the run blocking against the Jets? >> That's something we I think that's something we took a step forward in. You know, we were able to we were able to create some explosives, we were able to uh sustain some drives because of it. So it's something that we're just looking to build on. >> What have you seen from Mike in his development in the passing game both in pass pro and and routes? >> He's just he's somebody that continues to improve, really works his craft. He wants to get at each and every single thing he does, whether it's, you know, putting his hands up, his eyes, everything coming out. Um, you know, it's all the all the little fundamental things that that we talk about. It's stuff that he wants to get better at, improve on, and that'll that'll allow him to become a more successful player. >> Why do you feel there's a a contrast with Ashton where he's near the top of the league in receiving at the running back position, but then struggling running the ball through halfway almost halfway through the season? >> Well, running the ball is is a full team thing. Anything, you know, the greatest thing about football in general is that it's it's 11 as one on every single play. So it takes all 11 for everybody to be successful. So, you know, we really don't look at it as an individual statistic. We really look at it as us as an offense and, you know, where we're improving. Whoever is the uh whoever is the back carrying the ball, that's a that's a team statistic. So, you know, he's had some success as far as as receiving the ball and he's also been growing as a runner. We've been growing with him as a runner. So it's something that we want to just keep improving on and going forward with. >> You guys have tried to be pretty creative in the sneak game early in the season. This past week you kind of went just old school, let Kirk sneak it for the most part. I guess what did you see from him to be able to to do that in short yardage? >> I think that just that's something that, you know, he has a will and want to do. It was something that we saw on tape that was that allowed us to be successful. Things change week to week. Uh schemes change week to week, but that was what something we identified this past week that allowed us to allowed us to keep drives going, allowed us to score, allowed us to ultimately win the game. >> Seems the first one something he just he just called it at the line. It looked like he kind of audibled into that. >> Uh he I mean, he has things that he can get to, but we have play calls and it's different on every single time and every single uh you know, every every single scenario is different. >> Kirk said one of the coaching points is even if Brock Bowers is covered, you still throw in his direction. Was that something you guys like established like right away from the jump or it kind of like progresses you guys kept practicing? >> Kirk has a read and a progression to go through every time and he has a feel and it's something that we trust with him as far as his experience goes and it's something we trust with with Brock as far as, know, his skill set's concerned that when when Kirk feels like he's open, he's going to pull the trigger, and if not, he's going to go keep on his progression. >> What does Brock do for the offense even when he isn't getting the ball in in terms of spacing? >> Uh he's he's just a he's a tremendous talent, so he's somebody that we try to utilize a bunch of different ways, and he's a guy that he's a guy that's going to do everything full speed 100% of the time where he's first in progression, last in the progression, what what he's doing in the run game, what he's doing um you know, as far as if we ask when we ask him to block and um when we ask him to run routes, he just trying to do, you know, whatever he can do the best of his ability and be the best in the world at what he does. >> What do you think from the 49ers defense? >> Uh it's a talented bunch, been together for a long time, experienced bunch. It's a team that have a lot of familiarity with playing playing against them last year. They're well-coached, uh well-prepared. They attack the football. They, you know, they're very opportunistic, so it'll be a heck of a challenge for us against the, you know, one of the one of the best teams in the league. >> Kirk said it feels like every week you guys are going up against a top five defense in the league. I guess having that experience going into San Francisco, how does it help you guys as you go as you head up there? >> Yeah, I think, you know, we do our film study. They're going to do their film study on us. We're going to you know, find new and new and unique different ways to attack defenses. Uh it's a new play caller, so it's it's a new system as far as what we saw from last year. I know that some of the some of the players are the same and they're retooled, too. They've gotten uh they've gotten some new pieces. They they've gotten some guys back from injury, so that's something that, you know, we look forward to going on the road and using as a good measuring stick and and uh it's a heck of an opportunity, really. >> You coached against the the Raiders in Oakland a couple of times, correct? >> Yes. >> Uh what do you remember from those games playing in the Coliseum? >> Oh dang, that was uh I I was really young. Um I was really young in my my career then, but I just remember being a heck of an experience. Anytime you can Anytime you can talk about the Black Hole and and the Raider fans, that's something that's really unique and special. It's something that's really unique and special to the culture here in Vegas. Uh the history of the whole Silver and Black, shield, the black hole, those people. Uh, I remember as a visitor and as young as I was, and as young and experienced as I was, I was like, dog gone, this is this is a heck of an environment to come into. So, um, it was it's truly something that's that's unique to this franchise and this organization. So, we we look forward to seeing, you know, whatever Silver and Black get on the road with us. >> Last week, uh, Kubiak said that you guys were going to shift some things on the offensive line to find the right group of guys to see if you could fit there with Trey Zone getting his opportunity at right guard. How much did he contribute to maybe you guys finding that the right guys in that unit? >> I thought Trey came out and competed well. I thought they they gelled well. You know, Tyler does a great job of getting everybody on the same page. Uh, Rico and and Ben and Mario did a heck of a job getting those guys prepared, getting getting him up to speed, getting getting him ready to go. And then, uh, then the credit to Trey for going out and executing, doing stuff well, growing, uh, fixing mistakes on the field, and he'll continue to get better. >> Trey has been Trey Tucker has been one of your top receivers, but it's kind of been, you know, week by week in terms of his production. Do you think that it's defenses respecting him more as a player? Are you trying to find more ways to kind of consistently get him going? >> You're always trying to you're always trying to find, uh, your playmakers and put them in the best position possible to have success. And last week, while he the ball didn't find him as much, he was doing he was doing things away from the ball that were that were that were really good stuff that helped us be successful. That a guy I've never seen somebody, uh, so happy for his teammates to have success. So, that that's really the mark of somebody you're looking for to be on your offense. So, but you know anytime his number's called, he's going to be ready to go. And it's something that we try to we try to get him in the best position possible to be successful. >> What challenges does them adding DeForest Buckner to their defense present? >> Yeah, I mean, that's a that's a guy that's been that's been one of the top in the leagues of what he's done for a long time. So, it'll be a great challenge for us to you know, he's a heck of a player. Um, been doing it for a long time. He has the familiarity there with that group. Those guys know each other, so it won't be just like plugging a new player in, but you know, obviously that's a that's a a lot of talent added added to a very talented group. >> Thank you. >> Thanks guys. Have a good day. >> How you doing? >> Obviously, you know, the entire game probably wasn't what you wanted Sunday, but the second half you guys came up with stops and I guess how do you kind of evaluate the whole thing? >> Yeah, no, it wasn't wasn't pretty, you know, and there's a lot we have to fix. But, you know, been here a couple years and not many times we come out finding a way to win and I was proud of the resilience of getting hit in the mouth the first three plays and we we have a you know, red area stop on the three yard line. So there's a lot of points on the little things that helped us win that game that um and how they rallied in the fourth quarter. You know, it was really fun to see. >> Jamal McCoy got some extended reps with DP went down just how do you think he handled that situation? >> Good. Um some ups and downs, but you know, he's learning. He's very coachable. Um and competitive. I really like where he's at. >> You brought up the red area. I think they went two for six um in the red zone. Just where did you see improvements in in red zone defense? >> Just just overall, you know, in the um you know, all of it to get him to a four-point play, a third down, and then to execute was was nice and that's that's all we're looking for is to see improvement in certain areas and and trying to target a morning at time and and we did that. So so I was happy. >> They targeted Eric Stokes quite a bit on on Sunday. Was that something you guys were anticipating um ahead of the game and how do you think he handled that? >> No, I I think uh no, I mean, you know, they they their game plan was their game plan. I don't I don't know what their plan was. Um but you know, I think of the the four-point plays, the ones he did make that help that helped keep them to field goals. You know, and you playing corner, I thought he handled himself really well. >> They had so much success running the ball. They kind of abandoned that in the second half. Is there something you did not to take away the run, but to take away the looks that they might run into? >> Yeah, we tried to adjust, you >> obviously, you know, like I said, it was it was tough sledding. Like, you know, we need to be better and and um we talked about some things. It's hard to come like what what what their mindset was, but we we tried to fix some things and adjust. >> Even with those adjustments, you know, how much of it was, you know, schematic versus guys just playing harder in your opinion? >> When you have when you have multiple errors, which you know, we did, it's a combination of both, you know? And and and um making sure the guys are in the right spots or attacking certain things or um you know, and we have some guys playing in some different spots, so just just being clear on all those things. >> What have you seen from the 49ers offense, which obviously has a lot of guys in and out of injuries throughout the year, but they seem to keep on clicking throughout the year? >> Yeah, they do they do they're fundamentally sound, man. You know, they're they're a clean operation and and uh they got some good players, you know, and uh quarterback's playing at a high level, good tight end, running backs like they they and the offensive line is is really good. So um but they're that that's what jumps out to me, how fundamentally sound they are and they're able to put a lot of pressure on you. >> Schematically speaking with Clint's familiarity with the 49ers and kind of being over there, how much has that also helped you with that your defensive game plan with how much experience he has with them? >> Yeah, um a little bit, but that's it's it's consistent every week, but yeah, these definitely Clint's always helpful. Clint's always helpful in his perspective on anything. And uh yeah, he's been helpful. >> The last few weeks the guys have been saying it's all about doing your 111. Um is there anything else that maybe you were challenging them to do this week as you guys head up to face the 49ers? >> Um stack plays, really focusing on us, our alignment, our assignment, key technique, fundamentals, fundamentals. And you know, it's especially that time of the year of of where it's hard to really out out scheme people. Everybody knows who they are, so you have to go out and execute. And um yeah. >> You were with the the Giants in 2017 when they played the the Raiders at the Coliseum, right? >> 2017 I was there with yeah, the Genos game, yeah. >> So what what do >> remember about playing against the Raiders in Oakland? >> When we was with the Giants, this when we benched G-Live for the first time and Gino started. That's the first thing that sticks out, but the uh I mean, the environment was different. You know, it was awesome. You know, I was just so I remember standing at the 50 yard line. Uh wasn't a good experience for us, but it was a it was pretty cool for I mean, the Raider environment was awesome. It was awesome. >> Having been a part of this organization for the past few years, what does like this game going back to on the Bay Area for the first time in >> It's like you say, if you if you respect the game and understand how this thing really went down and what it you you know, what it was when they were means a lot to a lot of people and I think it's awesome to be a part of. It's very humbling and you know, we want to go and put on a performance that everybody's proud of, you know, as a team. >> What have you seen in practice that has earned Tim Kanan, you know, the the activations and the reps in the games? >> Yeah. Um he's stout. Um he's a pro. Again, I go back to all the traits you value of any good player being a leader. He's out there early. He's going through. He really embraces his role of what we're asking him to do and um I really like him. >> Go go back to Jamar. He said there was, you know, some good and some bad. That being away from football for so long, that 2024 film is is so good of his. Are you starting to see some of those traits show up again now that he's working his way back into the >> Yeah. I think you've seen traits of that since he got here and it's just him feeling through his process, you know, just watching and observing and seeing where he's at, but he he's flashed since he's gotten here in and out and you're looking for consistency. >> Good. >> Yeah. >> Cool. >> Thanks, guys. >> Appreciate it. >> Yeah, appreciate it, guys.

title: Aaron Donald, Puka Nacua & Rams Coordinators On Playing Connected, Week 9 vs. the Commanders & More
text: What is the loss of Jaylen for you guys? >> Yeah, it's obviously a big loss. Um, you know, it felt like he was really just hitting his groove. Um, he really became a connector in the DB room. He was getting the guys together. He asked great questions in the meeting room. So, um, it's a huge loss and, uh, you know, a lot of guys got to step up. We have, we have faith in the guys that are here and, you know, we're going to be next up, but you definitely feel for the person because he was having a great year. >> Practice, uh, I think that remains to be seen. What do you mean to get uh Miles Garrett back out on the practice field yesterday? >> It was it was great to see him. You know, he's been around. He's doing been uh in the meeting rooms, kind of learning the system, and it's been great to, you know, have him out there a little bit, be around the guys and get him running around. >> How do you What do you think he looked like yesterday? >> You know, he looked he looked like uh Miles Garrett, you know, so it was it was good to see him. Obviously, you know, limited reps and things like that, but uh good to have him out there. He obviously has a lot of experience and success in this league, but what are the challenges of not getting a lot of time during training camp with your teammates and then coming back in the middle of the season? >> Yeah, you know, and we always kind of knew that, you know, you obviously like to bank a lot of those reps throughout training camp, but you know, you're always going to deal with the the hand that you're that you're given and that's what we're going to do. So, you're going to, you know, try to value every single walkthrough rep, every single practice rep that we get with him and try to mesh his game with our defense together and try to find the best version for his game and and for the defense of the Rams. What uh as you watched Aaron's errant fumble recovery uh in act, what was your reaction as you were watching that? >> I mean, yeah. Um no, obviously you wanted him to scoop it and then you're, you know, whatever. But, uh it was funny. I told him, you know, I have I have a whole reel of clip of clips of guys over the years that, you know, bend, you know, sink your hips and scoop and score. And he was causing every fumble, doing it. And I was going to show it in camp, but it was the week he was about to come back. So, I was like, I don't want to show him causing all these fumbles. So, I told him I get to add him to the reel, you know, but just on the other side of it, you know, but obviously sink your hips and scoop it. >> Um, [snorts] you guys, uh, signed David Long to the practice squad. Can you explain, I think it's obvious, but maybe some of the background and why you decided to bring him in. >> Yeah, first of all, he's a great person, great teammate. Um, you know, I was with him really his whole time here, his last year. I was in the DB room with him and uh, you know, so a lot of fond memories with him. Uh, he's a true professional. I think he's a guy that some of the young guys can really lean on and talk to and get to know. I was actually telling Josh Wallace that he's a guy he should be picking his brain and talking through stuff. Uh he loves football. Um I think he might want to be a coach, but he uh um you know, he's had a great career this far and we were excited to have him back. He left a great impression here. >> Q and uh Trent both had interceptions last game and have continue to improve. How important are they going to be moving forward, especially with Jay now being out? Yeah, I mean either way they're obviously two of the key pieces of our defense. You know, Q Lake, you know, has obviously been the captain here for years or ever since I've I've been the coordinator. And then, you know, having Trent this year has been amazing and all the stuff he can do being able to move around. Really, both those guys being able to move around whatever you want to do. They're true guys that love football and uh they allowed you to get your best best 11 on the field and they set the example for exactly how we want to play and how we want the Rams defense to play and uh I we expect them to continue to do that. Anything else? >> When you lose a guy like Watson, you know, h how do you have him uh kind of help contribute even though he's not on the field? I mean, you kind of talked about in the meeting rooms, you know, you got a couple young guys in in the position group. How does he help contribute even though he's not >> Yeah, exactly what you said in the meeting room um taking the guys under his wing at the practice field. Um, we I always loved about him is he was always he was never afraid to ask ask a tough question in the meeting room and so you always felt like if you know he understood it. You knew if he didn't know he was going to ask the question and you know when he gets back in there that's what you know we're going to expect from him where hey you try to understand it like you're playing the game in the meeting room and uh ask those questions exactly the same just like you're playing and to help all these guys and help the room just like he's been doing. >> Q had the dot again last week. Was that more just maintaining continuity or did that have to do a part with um you know Lman's first game back? >> I think it's just you know you're always kind of taking it week by week. Um I you know I wouldn't say continuity. It's just you're always going to do what's best for that week. Again I always say you'd like for it to be on the second level and uh just depending on what it is, but a lot of it depends on the game plan and who we expect to be out there. >> All right. Thanks. >> Thanks. >> Appreciate it guys. >> Thanks. What's up guys? What was it like to have Terrence back in practice yesterday? >> It was good. It was good seeing him back out there. I know he's been chomping at the bit to to get back out on the field and obviously getting him rolling. I think Reggie and their staff do a great job of just having a plan whenever we're kind of getting those guys back into the rhythm, back into the flow. Uh but good to have him out there. Good to see him moving around and you know excited for him to stack another day hopefully today. >> I know you guys you've still been through the 13 a lot, but what does having him specifically back help for that room? >> Yeah, I think the more of those guys available the better we're going to be. We obviously have a lot of confidence in each of those guys and the versatility they bring. Um and and obviously the elements that Ferg has been able to bring during his career here. Um but certainly been encouraged by the guys that have been in there um even in his absence. You know, seeing Max Clair on the field last week. Uh obviously Kobe Parkinson when he's been healthy has has made a huge impact for us. Uh Davis Allen and his consistency, Tyler Higgby, those guys have all done a really good job. Uh so I think the more of those guys that you have available and adding to the fold, the better you're going to feel. you talked about um you know a conversation you had with Tutu about him being like the ultimate assist man or something like that. Yeah. Um so what was it like to see him you know >> football you know it's just it's deserving and it's what happens in football you uh you know you commit to the right things. You do what's best for the team. Uh and good things end up you know coming to you in that way. So, it wasn't a surprise that a play like that was going to show up. For him to kind of spark us, uh, for him to make a couple plays last week that I thought were huge for us, um, you know, in conversion situations, obviously, to get us going and and provide points on that two-minute drive there. Um, you know, it was huge for us and and it'll be something that'll continue to come to life, but I think that's that's just how the game works, you know, and and you do the right things and you commit to that, uh, good things follow. >> Is he a guy that you'd like to get the ball to more, and if so, what's the process of making that happen? Yeah, he definitely is and he's a guy that's shown up um you know and had just just that consistency with Matthew over the course of his career that I think Matthew has a lot of comfort with. And so uh I think with all those guys you're you're always trying to figure out the best ways to activate them uh to get them rolling. Um you know and we feel confident of their ability to impact the offense uh when when that shows up. You know, it's it's a week toeek thing and and exactly how you're going to utilize them, exactly how everybody's how that ball is going to get distributed. But we got a lot of confidence in those guys to be able to make plays. >> Nate, it seems like whenever you guys have gone tempo this season, whether it's two-minute drills or what have you, the offense finds that spark immediately, even if you didn't have it before. Why does that allow you guys to to hit that next gear? You know, I think that you have a lot of guys that have continuity with each other that in moments where there's chaos on the field, where calls are coming in quick, where you're going to have to make quick decisions as a quarterback, uh that they got a lot of clarity on where people are supposed to be, um that they got a lot of clarity on, you know, exactly how they're supposed to be there. Uh and just the timing and the rhythm rhythm has been uh on point in that way. So, uh, it's been awesome to see because obviously in in the NFL you're going to have, you know, drives specifically at the end of the game where, uh, yeah, we're going to need those guys to be at their best and and so for them to show up like that in those kind of ways throughout the course, it's it's been great. And, um, yeah, it's something to be able to build on. >> How important is Puka in those types of situations as someone that Matthew has a lot of trust in can go to like that? Yeah, I mean, Puka is just one of those guys that he finds a way to make plays over and over again. And whether that's down the field, whether that's underneath, whether that's getting yards after the catch, whether that's putting the ball in his hands in the in the run game. Um, he's he's found a way to make plays uh since he has been in the NFL and certainly before that. But, um, I think you said it, the the word trust and and having the quarterback's trust to be at the right spot, uh, in the right moment. You know, that that's what it comes down to at at the receiver spot and certainly in this offense. >> Puka this season has dealt with the hip injury and the calf injury and you said both times he felt like his explosiveness wasn't quite there. When you see Puka now on the field, do you see that explosiveness or is it something he's going to deal with all this? Yeah, you know, that's always something that I think guys as they are dealing with injuries, there's going to be parts of their game that they feel like aren't, you know, to maybe their own standard. I I've still seen a guy that's that's been able to be um, you know, explosive when we've, you know, asked him to do that and relied on him to do that. And so, uh, but it's always that, you know, that first day of training camp, you kind of look at the guys and, you know, like, man, this is the last day that you're going to feel, you know, probably like you do right now. And so, there there's different things that they're, you know, dealing with throughout the course of the year. Um but but that being said, we we feel like he still is a player that uh has been explosive um and and and been just a guy that finds a way. Like I I just, you know, I think about the plays that he's made and and whether he feels tiptop 100% or whether he's um you know, a few percentage points down from that, he he just finds a way, which is which is what you appreciate about him. when he's dealing with these injuries, what's the balance for you and making sure you take advantage of all he can do but maybe not putting so much on it when Devonte is out and there's that injury risk factor. >> Yeah, there's a there's a balance. There's a balance that that happens not only on a Sunday u but even throughout the course of a of a practice week and I think the encouragement that we have is we have guys that we feel that we can put, you know, trust in uh to be able to supplement him in the right ways. you know, guys like Jordan Whittington, uh guys like Kate Mumfield, um even CJ Daniels that they've been able to step up and um you know, provide some of the elements that obviously we lean on Puka with, but also add their own spin on on what they do and what they bring to the table. And so that that's that's the best thing we got going in that receiver room, even with a guy like Devonte being out that we got other guys that we feel confident um you know, putting on the field in in a number of different ways. >> I think those three guys you mentioned have two catches combined in the past two weeks. So, I guess how do you get more out of them if you aren't going to, you know, lean on them? >> Yeah, you you know what, it's it's a it's a age old, you know, football. There's a number of different ways to impact uh the game. And certainly catching the ball is one of those, you know, things that receivers enjoy and appreciate doing. But I think what's cool about this building is there's a lot of appreciation for um all the different ways that you can impact. And you know, even not having Puka for a couple of those games, it's like, yeah, man, you you you know, miss seeing him catch the football, but there's a lot of those, hey, insert blocks in the run game. Um, you know, the ability to, you know, uh, get a jet sweep handoff, th those things that, uh, may not show up in the stat sheet as as a catch, uh, but are big parts of our offense. And so, um, you know, we definitely feel good about those guys being able to catch the football, but, uh, you know, with a 60 70 play game, there's going to be a lot that we require them to do. and we feel like those guys can step up and do all those things. >> I know you coach on the other side of the ball, but when you see Aaron Donald around and see the way he works, what's your impression? Yeah, it's been really cool because I was, you know, I came here as a Ram uh post, uh, Aaron Donald, um, you know, round one, you know, I'm I'm only a part of round two. And so, uh, I had a lot of excitement, you know, when he first hit the field just to to see what it would look like. And I think um probably not even that from a football standpoint, but just you know who he is, how he carries himself and and have heard so many stories since being here about what he's like, the mentality that he brings to just attacking every day, staying present in the moment, and you know, requiring greatness from everyone around him. And so I've been I've been encouraged to be around him. It's been cool to see and obviously cool to see him make plays on the field um that are uniquely, you know, geared towards him. And so, um, yeah, it's been an awesome experience for me as a coach to see a player like that, um, you know, do his do his thing. >> What does it say about him that before he got he came back for round two and you you heard those stories and he was talked about that way in this building? Yeah, you know, reputation precedes who he is and what he's about. And I think, you know, it's it's the impact that he made from, again, even that that round one, uh, I think was felt by everyone that had been around him, by the stories that had been told, uh, whether it's an offseason training camp story, you know, Sean telling it in in the year after Aaron had retired in my first year here, it was like, man, that's that's wired into the fabric of this building. and you know in a lot of ways will probably always be um you know because of the the approach that he took again not just the plays that he made on the field but the approach he uh took on on 365 days a year uh to what it looked like to be you know at his best and so that that's that's as impactful that's as much about a person and and their career and their impact as as anything. >> What was that story Sean told you? The story Sean told me uh us was um you know it was about controlled aggression and the importance of learning that and I think it was something you'd have to ask AD about it but I think it was something that he learned over the course of his career and impacted him in a way where he was he was utilizing it in the in the most important moments. I think there's stories before that where he may have not utilized that, you know, as well as he would have liked to, but again, I wasn't here for that. Um, I'm just hearing the the positive story of what, you know, what came to be. Um, you know, but controlled aggression, that's what it was all about. And he seems like a guy that is all about that, you know, one way or another. >> Appreciate you guys. Yep. >> Did you get a chance to obviously you're doing your own thing out there in practice today. check out Terrence Ferguson and what he looked like today in his return. >> Um, yeah, we got a chance. We come out in the in the second warm-up, so we got to warm up together, ask him how he's feeling and the the confidence I think the pep in his step what said more than he could have said to me. Obviously, he said he's feeling great. Obviously ready to be out there. Um, but I thought in our routes on air and Indie and then the reps that he's got out there, it looks like Ter obviously he's got some stuff that he's working through, but uh you can see in his movement pattern when he's being able to put his foot in the ground, it feels confident. It looks confident. what is what would have him impact? >> I think um T Fergus is obviously somebody allows us to to pass the ball in our 13 personnel um with him being a vertical threat, but also I'm like the toughness that is in that tight end room um is in each individual tight end that we send out there. So, it'll be exciting. I know he's excited to show everybody that uh he's ready to hit somebody, but also get out there and create some space for our offense and uh catch catch the ball and get ready to run. >> Couple years ago, you guys [clears throat] played the Browns at Sofi Stadium. Do you have any recollections of trying to block Miles Spirit in that game or going against? >> Um, luckily I I I I don't think I had to in that game. Um, I know Alec Jackson definitely had the task and I'm like I think uh I mean I don't know if Miles has seen the clip since we've been back, but I know we showed it after we beat them of of Kairen being able to put his face mask on him. So, uh um that was something I'm glad I like my physicality and but I'm like I'm glad I didn't have to have a block 95 out there and I'm glad he's in in our colors now. [laughter] Hookah, how does the the run game in this like two-headed attack between Kairen and and Blake scored touchdowns in the last two games each of them opened up your game as well between more manageable situations I guess in like third and short. So, >> um yeah, I think it's it's something I'm like we pride ourselves in the in the wide receiver room just staying connected. Um uh trusting those backs. Um I know something that Coach G is always coming up like this right around after our Wednesday install. I'm like he comes around and say, "Hey, you ready to put your face on somebody?" And that's something I think we pride ourselves in. And when those guys uh break off for explosives, I think that's that's we take that that's a that's a play that we don't get contributed for. There's no stats that show up for us unless you pancake somebody. But uh it's something that we take pride in. When you see those guys run past you, um that means we got connected on the safeties or whatever defender might be there. So they both have their own style and it's really been really fun to see them both go at it and uh that combination of the two cuz uh I'm sure as a as a defense you don't enjoy seeing some fresh legs come in and then getting ready to run downhill again. quickly. Uh Mick Cross in terms of alignment is probably the most versatile or has been asked to do the most things in the secondary across the NFL.
