So, I think it's a it's a it's a great credit to them, uh their their ability to communicate and it's going to be a challenge for us to to be able to be uh where we need to be in the timing of our and rhythm of our plays with the different challenges and the the presentations they give us. So, it'll be an exciting challenge and obviously AM Robinson is somebody that we've had a chance to see last year in Detroit. So, um somebody that we're somewhat familiar with and knows and knows our offense, but um new year, new opportunities for us. So, it'll be exciting to go out here and put a put some new stuff on tape on Sunday. >> How much pride do you take in being physical in the Red Game and I know that was something that's been really emphasized throughout your time here. Just talk to me a little bit about what that's like for you. >> Um where do I start? Uh no, I'm like taking me back to 2023 training camp, but no, I'm just kidding. Uh but no, I I enjoy it. I'm like I I can't uh growing up playing football, I'm like the head on a swivel is is a phrase that I heard all growing up playing the game of football. And I think uh especially now being in the NFL, I'm like the room for error is so small. Guys are moving fast. I'm like there's 11 guys. It's the same size football field we've been playing on since kids. Uh it's just people cover a lot more ground than they did in pew football. So um it's exciting. So to be able to catch a defender when they're not looking and and being in our cues and like we mentioned when our when our backs are are cutting off our tails and being able to make our blocks right makes it really fun. when we can catch a defender with his feet off the ground, um drive him into the dirt or just um like there's every once in a while I get to hit a backer when he's not looking. So, I enjoy that one because like it sets a tone for me and then especially for our offense when you see bodies hitting the floor and here comes our um our our style of back who's a little bit shorter than everybody else just freaking running through the hole at full speed. It makes it really fun to block. >> Thank you guys. >> Thank you. >> I can't complain. phone's. >> Hey Aaron, so uh Miles Garrett is back at practice. What are you excited about sharing the field with them? >> Well, it's good to have the pieces back to the puzzle. Um was good to see him out there yesterday. Today looking good, looking fast. Um getting to work with them and and full pads and playing off each other. Looked pretty good today. So, um I'm excited about having him here, having him back obviously and and see what he do Sunday. So, >> what was going through your mind as you tried to pick the fumble up on the field? >> A touchdown. I thought I was going to score, but it ain't go that way, you know. So, just got to be better at that. So, um you know, missed the ball, laid there for a minute, felt silly as hell, and and that was that. But, you know, I got to be better. So, >> looked like you were at the front of the line when you were doing the scoop drills today. >> Yeah, that was my I needed I need that. I need that learn bending getting down. Um so, when opportunity present itself again, I take advantage of it. So, >> have you seen all the re like Sean said you couldn't look him in the eye? You had Miles laughing on the bite. You got >> this. I'm I'm going to explain to you exactly what I seen. Boom. I seen a ball. First thing came my head. Touchdown. I'm going to get this ball. I should have slowed down, but I felt people behind me like I want to get hit my back. That's going [laughter] to hurt. So, I tried to go full speed and scoop it. The ball was going I thought the ball was going to bounce this way, but it bounced that way. And it just looked at all damn silly. And that's and I was like, "Ah." [laughter] And then I hit the ball out and I just laid there. I can't believe I just did that. So when I seen it, the first thing popped in my head was I got my first touchdown. That's what I was thinking. But it ain't play out like that. So >> but you get a kick out of the reaction. It's like even Stafford was miked up saying it's hard for us guys. >> And man, I seen everything everybody. Okay. >> My older brother called me was like, "Man, [laughter] how you missed your touchdown, man? We've been talking about that." But you know, like I said, man, if it present itself to me again, I just got to take advantage of it and and pick it up this time and try to do something with it. So >> Sean, jumping. He's going to give you a lot of crap for that. That happened this week. >> He sent me a test that night and joked about it, but um you know, a lot of guys joked about it, but and um be honest, I was a little upset with it, you know, cuz you know, could have put some more points on the board, at least got the ball back for offense in the short field. So, um I got to be better, you know. So, um it's all fun games cuz we won, but you know, if it was a different situation and we didn't win, it'd be a lot worse. So, um, you know, just got to keep working, keep being better at the little things and and not let stuff like that happen. So, >> you guys have another mobile quarterback and Jaden Daniels this week. Obviously, Josh Allen few weeks ago rushed for like over 100 yards against you. Jaden's had over 100 against the Giants earlier. How do you keep him in the pocket? Let him do what? >> We got a good game plan. We've been talking about it. Cleaning up some things up front that we can do better off playing with each other, playing off each other, I should say. Um, to not allow him to, you know, gash us and hurt us. you know, I'm pretty pretty sure he going to get his get a couple plays here and there, but um as long as we kind of keep him contained, keep him in the pocket, not let him get them big rush lanes where he can just take advantage of um we'll be fine. But um great football player, dynamic quarterback, and we just got to find ways to affect them. So, >> if uh and when Miles does come back, do you anticipate that's going to free you up a little bit more from some of the different blocking schemes? Um, I'm pretty sure it's and the guy did have 20 something sacks last year, but you know, I'm going to go out there just play. We all going to just play. Um, if Miles is 100% ready to go and he play this week, that's going to be amazing for us. Great. Cuz like I said, it's always good when you got all the pieces to the puzzles out there. So, um, hopefully he's feeling great after, you know, the day at practice and come in feeling good and he can go Sunday and then we can go out there and execute, you know, the game plan and play with each other and, um, and try to have some success. too. >> AD, >> you guys have managed to fall back to four and four. Um, after a slow start, when you reflect being at this at this point, why is adversity important uh throughout the course of the season? >> Well, there's no way to avoid it. It's going to be ups and downs in a football season or it just happened to happen early. Um, like I said before, it was nothing to panic about. You know, we just got to keep playing good ball week in and week out, trying to find ways to, you know, stay together. even though the outside world saying whatever they saying, as long as we stay connected inside and we just continue to work through the adversity that's going to happen in football, there's no way you can, you know, go around it. It's just that's what that's a part of the game. Um, and continue continue to stick together, continue to play this game. Um, good things come from it, but we just got to continue to work. Um, go one week at a time and and keep trying to stack wins. So, >> and then Jayen Watson, he he's out for the year for the show. Emanuel Forks more than likely is getting ready into that that position. When you look at the totality of the secondary Q, the year he's having Trent, um Cam Kitchens, can you just talk to me about the secondary? Have you ever played with the secondary of this caliber? >> I played with some good guys, but you know, there been some playmakers back there that's playing some good ball right now. And you know, obviously when you lose a good player, you got another guy to step up that you trust and it's always next man up, right? um understanding that, you know, the guy that's going to step in is g it's not gonna be too big of a drop off. Um and and and it feel good when you got guys on the back end that you can trust, right? Um I had some years where I played with some really good football players that played on the back end where you knew they be able to hold the ball a little longer and you get some opportunities to get after the quarterback and it's like it feel like that again, you know, and obviously having all the pieces to the puzzle coming back this week hopefully um we'll go out there and execute um execute this game plan we got in this week, man. I think it can be fun. So, I'm excited about it. Um, you know, just ready to go out there and play some ball. So, >> talk to you. >> You seem a little bit looser than maybe the first time we covered you. Do you know >> when since when you >> Okay, maybe I just didn't want to talk to y'all or something. I don't [laughter] know. Maybe I miss y'all. That's probably what it is, huh? >> I guess my question, it seems like a noticeable difference. I'm curious. Do you have a different perspective coming here back around than maybe you did? >> No, I'm just I'm just having fun, man. That's it. um 35 years old playing football. It's a kids game. We know obviously you going to have them aches and pains. It's like I miss my hands now hurting, my body all achy, but um you still get to go out there and play this game and had the opportunity to be out here today. I'm just I'm just enjoying having fun and maybe I just miss you guys, man. And like to joke around with you guys a little bit. So, >> especially Gary, >> huh? >> Especially Gary. [laughter] >> One more question for sports. Uh can you tell me at this point in the season you're halfway there like is it what you expected? >> It's never going to be what you expected. You know from the beginning where where it started that nothing played out how I thought it was but you can't control that. You know once you make a commitment it's like you got your vision you kind of think what can happen and it's like what you think can happen. It's like it was a whole 360 of how everything played out for me. And I don't got to go into detail in details as as far as that. But um no, it's not what I expected, but we here and I'm going join it though, you know. I'm enjoying it. Um I'm enjoying the process. I'm enjoying myself week and week out getting better. I'm enjoying being out there with the guys. Um you know, and just playing this game. So ain't what I expected, but I'm enjoying it.

title: LIVE: The Houston Texans address the media
text: tall was standing there when it comes to uh trying to unlock Nico Collins and when they're doing the coverage as they did, especially what New York tried to do. What are some ways to try to get him more involved? Kind of what's the goal? What's the hope for trying to get Nico more touches? >> Yeah, I think the goal is always to to make him a focal point of our offense. I think being able to move him around. Um, being able to do some different things with him positionally, um, you know, schematically and just trying to put him in different spots. Um, certainly, you know, I can do a better job of that. Um, but we we're always going to, you know, have Nico as a focal point. Um, he's a huge part a piece of what we do obviously. Um, so that's always the focal point for us. >> When it comes to the jumbo package, you run it twice as much as the second most team >> in the league. You're one of only three teams to have five tight ends on the roster. Why so much jumbo? And this week, De Mo says about imposing your will, win the run game, but you also have to pass out of it. It's mixed signals here on on why this package is so prevalent. >> Yeah, I would just say this. It is week to week. I mean, there's certain times from a a grouping standpoint, what we're trying to how we're going to combat different front structures, um what advantages we feel it may or may not give us from week to week. Um and then, you know, it ties into a bunch of different things like relative to, you know, run game protections. we can do a lot of different things out of it. Um I think it's you know we've used it a decent amount. You're you're not wrong in that at all and I think just you know it has helped us in moments and I think that you know we've got you know quite a bit of I would say skilled players too to be able to offset some things. So the key is just trying to have balance and I feel like you know if I just start with myself like I'm always going to do like probably didn't get into any kind of rhythm that I would have liked to last game and not mixing the groupings as much as obviously I would have hoped for. So just got to do a better job of that. What is the game plan for uh Tank Dale this week? >> Yeah, just have him be him. I mean, he he has versatility. He can play really all three spots um for us. Um so there's been no restrictions from that and you know, I think he's done a really good job of just being on top of all the details and and we'll be able to utilize him and and you know, be able to move him around in in quite a few places if needed. >> Were the snaps increased with Jaylen No being out? >> Yeah, I mean I believe I believe so. Uh, you know, again, I'm not going to ever sit there and say like one thing definitively because you never know how these games go. But yeah, he's he's picking up steam and I would say like he's done a great job, you know, dating back to the time we had his window opened up for us. >> How I guess uh devastating was it to lose Jaylen uh the way he did, especially as he was starting to really develop? >> Yeah, I think you know, you always feel feel obviously you feel terrible for for the guy. He made a lot of progress. He's a hard worker. Um I was really proud of the the gains he had made. um just continuing to get better and I think I said it a couple weeks back just gaining more confidence being able to go out there and just build off of things from week to week and I was really proud of him. Um and so you know you you you feel bad for the player because he's a team guy and wants to be out there with us. Um but he'll be back. He'll be back strong and he'll work his ass off to to get back but certainly feel for for a guy like that. What's >> your overall assessment of the offense when heading into the by week coming out of the B? >> Yeah, I think we just got to do a better better job of just playing clean. Okay. Going forward and and staying on schedule more and you know again starting with myself, starting with the staff, starting with and then down to the players and all of us just continue to be more efficient. Uh uh eliminate unforced errors, the pre- snap penalties and things like that and try to play our cleanest game and go out and compete and play our cleanest game for 60 minutes and polish some of the things that we need to work on here moving forward. you know, eliminate the penalties, clean up some of the techniques, um, and, you know, see some different things that we can put some guys in different positions here and try to, you know, try to move the needle in some different areas there. >> Any progression behind the scenes for Marlon Klein? >> I missed the first, uh, >> any any progression behind the scenes for Marlon Klein? We don't see him in the games obviously inactive, but you're seeing from Marlin, anything that he's doing to inch toward? >> Yeah, no, he's he's made a lot of progress. I mean, all those guys I feel have done a good job. James Tren does a really good job with those guys. He's getting better every single week and again like you it's like anything else just focusing on the process trying to get better putting him in different situations getting him exposure to different areas in the C gap or off the ball run game and then being able to move them around. It's like anything else it's it's a continuous build for for a guy like him but it is for for all of us. >> The process of deciding the formations and stuff. You talked about the team coming together, no egos and stuff like at what point do y'all decide like hey maybe we should run some jumbo this week or maybe no 13 and 12 which we've talked about in the past like what is the process and when do y'all decide that? >> I mean it's through the week of the game plan like it's it's you look at you start looking at the opponent on Monday evenings you work through the game plan on you know base downs call it through Tuesday um you try to finalize that you know midday Tuesday into you know dinnertime and that's that's that's just for early downs. So, it's all segmented in terms of the progression and the flow of the week. And that's when you decide from a game plan standpoint, um a roster usage standpoint, etc., what we're going to do. That's pretty standard, I would say, in terms of how we're building the the game plan, what packages we're going to deploy, what we're going to see, how what groupings elicit certain responses from defensive personnel groupings, etc. throughout the week. >> Who is who is we? because it feels like you come up here and you take all the stuff, but you say it. McDaniels has said it. We've heard people say it like who are you who's around that table when this decision is >> and it's a staff. It's it's it's a staff >> part of this. >> It's a staff. It's we we as a as a as an offensive staff. Okay. We have our areas of responsibility. It's been like that every place I've been where, you know, people have certain responsibilities, but collectively we come together and when we talk through the the the game plan and what we want to ultimately do and ultimately I'll make the decision on how we're going to go ahead and what we're going to put on the call sheet. You you don't have a finite amount of calls that you're going to bring into a game really, but that's that's going through the process of studying the film, studying the defense, and being able to see what we feel helps us, you know, gives us the best chance to have success and put our guys in best position. >> Is Ceracio's in there, too? >> No, it's an offensive. I'm talking as an offensive staff. is not an offensive staff. >> He's not an It's our offensive staff. >> Uh I know last year you guys were more of a um kind of not I'll say it wrong, but you all were more of a kind of take care of the football um type of team. And not that you all aren't this year, but you all have have an uptick in explosive play. So what is the balance in in trying to make sure you try to take care of the football and trying to hit explosives when you can or trying to do more of that? I I think from a starting point standpoint before you talk about any plays, you talk about ball security and you talk about you talk about possessing the football and not giving defenses opportunities to steal possessions. So, you know, you look back, I was proud of last year. I think this year we're near the top of the league in terms of fewest fewest giveaways. Um, I'm proud of that. I think the guys are really conscientious. I think before any play, run, pass, whatever you're doing. I think it's paramount to be able to protect the football and I that extends to protection from an offensive line standpoint, chipping the edges, being friendly as a route runner to win the catch point. It's everything and it really encompasses all 11. So that's a starting point. And you talk about the aggressiveness and stuff like that. You know, we we you you understand the importance when the ball if we're pushing the ball down the field to go be aggressive to win at the catch point. But before that happens, you have to have a pocket established. You have to have the quarterback be able to have step up in the pocket and be able to deliver an accurate football. The routes have to be at the right depth, etc. So for us, it's all those things. Um, and I think when you talk about like being able to push the ball down the field, I think CJ, uh, you know, has done a good job with the offense of being able to bring all those things to life and and you know, and it's trust, right? It's being able to trust the guys that you're delivering the ball to down the field and then being able to protect the football. So, if if we're talking about in the pass game pushing it a little bit more down the field, it's trust that whoever, you know, we have the protection and when the ball goes up, the it's going to be us or nobody and we're going to protect the football and I think our guys have done a really good job of that um, and have embraced that. I don't have I don't have a stat for this, but watching you all play over the first seven games on the offensive side of the ball, it looks like when you all get into short yardage plays, you tend to run to the right a lot. And um is that behind Brown and behind Ingram instead of running maybe to Arante and to Keelin? Is that because of the experience or is that just something that you all feel more comfortable with? Like I said, I don't have the stats of how many times you've ran to that side, but it looked >> No, I'm going to say like, you're probably not right in terms of being more right-handed in terms of generally speaking, but, you know, I think most of the time it's more coincidental. There are some game plans throughout the, you know, my career, the last year and a half here, where we'll end up going, okay, where where do we know certain guys are going to be? How can we attack them, etc. And that's not just on early or not just on short, it could be on early downs, could be in goal line situations, too. But that's what we're trying to do. We're always trying to find out what gives us the best advantage in those situations and how can we go and some plays are alerted, you can go either way with it, etc. >> The Chargers right now running something similar to what you're seeing on a daily basis of a two linebacker set, you know, is it give you any benefit at all in any way to kind of see positionally, you know, or is it just, hey, week to week, scout to scout? >> I think it's week to week, scout to scout, like what are they doing out of those sets? What, you know, what pressures are they bringing? You know, what types of of of blitz zones were they aligning? Are they getting guys? Are they walking guys up and mugging them? Yeah. Yeah, coach is on enough of a hot seat. Uh, Norse code final season causing causing the bit apocalypse. Just show Spencer Brown the midterm results and he might get too upset to play. That's a good idea. He was already on on on uh on injured well, not injured reserve, but he was already too injured to play last week, so that'd be perfect. >> We'll get right on it. Good night.

title: LB Coach Al Washington meets with the media | Miami Dolphins
text: you were with Notre Dame last year. It's a big topic of conversation this week. Notre Dame uh Miami. How would you characterize maybe the motivation uh that is is over there after facing them last year and then also the CFP selection uh in the end? >> Yeah, I [snorts] mean I think their motivation is is to be honest, it sounds cliche is just to to be the best version of themselves. I think at that place and a lot of schools like that, um, when you kind of get lost in in what everyone else is saying and all the other things that don't really matter, you kind of lose, um, your ability to stay in the moment and stay focused. So, knowing that program, um, being a part of that program, I can tell you that's the focus. those guys are focused on what they need to do and, you know, trying to, you know, block out as much of the outside, you know, uh, opinions as possible because it really doesn't matter. What matters is kind of what you do in that moment, you know. So, it's coachy, but that's like, you know, that's my thought on it. >> You got a prediction on the game? >> Yeah, Notre Dame. No doubt. [laughter] >> Yeah. Without >> starting with that. >> Yeah. Yeah. as you look at you look at Jacob's season now obviously [snorts] through seven games you would characterize it how good great solid >> yeah you know this is my first round um but it's it's gone really well I mean I think statistically you look at his numbers and you say man this guy's has a a bright future but I think the things you guys may not be able to see like his command uh his leadership traits uh how much is is really like to be a linebacker in the NFL there's a a lot of responsibilities. It's like a quarterback on offense. And so, not only do you need to master what you need to do, you need to understand and have an appreciation for what others are doing. And with the green dot responsibility, you know, you have to communicate the call. He's the he, you know, he is that uh communicator. So, I just think as a rookie, man, um he's done a phenomenal job, but even, you know, just as a player, man, as a young man, he's uh he's done a hell of a job. And to stay on topic precisely, Jacob Rodriguez got the nomination uh from the Dolphins for Salute to Service. Have you had a chance to talk with him after that announcement? Just what that represents? Obviously, we know his ties with the military service, his dad Joe, his uh wife as well. So, just what what does it mean for one of your boys to get that nomination? Well, listen. Um, when after the meeting, I know he was humbled, you know, really appreciative. And I think he, um, you know, his wife, Emma, like the sacrifice they're making, right? She's in another country. He's embarking in this new journey. Um, and they stay in contact, but it can't be easy uh for either person. So, I think it's just uh I think it's a really nice um, you know, honor, I should say. probably a better way to say it's an honor for him and something that he doesn't take lightly and uh you know I think it's really cool because it's a lot of lot of sacrifice >> and also Jordan Brooks um the first week I was able to ask him about JRod and he said the sky is the limit for him what have you seen uh from Jacob after eight weeks >> yeah just uh I just see his growth like he's growing in a lot of different ways he's becoming more vocal um and I think this the speed of the game uh he's becoming more accustomed to not to say he was out of sorts at any point early in the year, but I just think the normal growth that would occur when you when you have time on task, you're starting to see and uh so I think sky's is the limit. You know, Jordan's a great person to kind of give that opinion. He's obviously had a great career and he's done a great job kind of wrapping his arm around him. Uh so it's really cool to see those two work together, but I agree with him. He's done a hell of a job. >> We had seen Jacob throw some of those peanut punches in this time successfully. What made that instance. What made what made that one the one that that worked? >> Well, listen, uh I think the circumstance like the ball was checked down. We stress uh ball out break, right? We want to be able to drive on the on the check down. And if you notice, Kaou was there as well. Uh and it's a collaborative deal like Kou kept leverage. Kyle Lewis, he kept leverage on the back on the on the checkdown and then Jacob pursuing kept his leverage and he happened to be to the side of the football. And we stress that every day, right? Wendell Davis, uh, assistant linebacker, coach does a great job kind of talking to the team on a regular basis about the importance of focus, finite focus on the ball. But yeah, I think the reason that happened that time is because the circumstance presented it, but it's second nature. And I in college, he was a machine, you know, I think it was in him, but it was really cool to see and it was a critical moment in that game that uh that we got to continue, you know, I think we got to continue to to get those uh opportunity, take advantage of those opportunities. >> I got a a play action question. about your guys. Hopefully I asked this correctly, but >> the trio of Jared Goff and Jir Gibbs and Sam Leaport, you guys faced, I guess, something similar against San Francisco maybe with with Perie and and CMC and KD. >> What does that do to your guys? What kind of quandry does that put your guys in? >> Yeah, listen, um, when you look at the Detroit Lions, I'll start with his head coach, the head coach, um, really fine coach from afar. You respect the way he operates. you look at their personnel, there's really no weaknesses. You brought up Gibbs, you brought up G, you you know, you brought up um Laaporta. Those three guys, like in the play action world, you know, they're critical to to having success for them. So, um we got to do a good job obviously on our end executing the defense that's called, but we got to be ready to make the plays when when they're presented, man. And so, um they just don't have any drop off, you You know, I think those all three of those guys are really good players. Uh, and you know, I think they impact the game on offense for them. >> Are are there keys that you can give to us that your guys should be reading without giving away strategy? >> Yeah, I just think you have to you really have to to be disciplined in your job. Like every call that's made, man, everybody has a job and issues come up a lot of times when you lose focus on that. And I think we got to commit to that and trust our preparation and and that gives you a chance. You know, you could do all that and you still got to make the tackle and uh but that is kind of the key. All right. We have to really master what we can control and compete our tails off and enjoy it. You know, it' be you know, it's a great opportunity and you know, that's kind of my opinion on that. >> Obviously, we know Jir is a is a great running back. Um but kind of talk to me a little bit about what he can do as a pass catcher and how that puts stress on your guys. >> Yeah, so like you look at the red zone, he has like you know 40 targets in the red zone like whether he's c, you know, catching the ball, running the ball, uh check down world. So I think he's a skilled athlete. He's got good ball skills. Um now because of what they have like they don't they probably don't need to ask him to get out and play slot as much because of the talent, but he could. You know, I just think he's a complete player and he's got great contact balance. like he's, you know, he's not a a Dererick Henry type stature, right? He's not a big bruising back, but you watch Tate, man, you know, uh he often he's breaking tackles. He's very explosive, got great contact balance. Um I think he's elite in that area. So, I think in the pass game checkdown world, when he has the ball in his hands, man, he's he's really effective, man, because of those things. >> We know that Kyle Lewis has been mostly in the safety room, but how long how many minutes do you spend with him each week? Um, you know, it depends on the week. Um, yeah, but he's he's um, you know, been uh been doing a lot of work with the back end and things like that because of his skill set. That's something we knew coming in. And fortunate for for us and him, like we spent the b the bulk of his first couple months was with the the LB room. So, I think he has a really good understanding of what that world's like. And now he's getting a chance to experience the back end. It's going to help him be a more complete player. you know, he's kind of like a Swiss Army knife. Really good player. So, uh, credit him for picking it up and and, uh, working working at it. >> What is pleased you the most about working with Jackson Woodard? >> Oh, man. Um, listen, Jackson is is the the very dependable person uh, and player. I think he's tough. He's rugged. Um, I appreciate the fact that you can count on him. You know, you can depend on him. and uh you know he he stepped in as you guys know a couple weeks ago and uh and you know he's whatever he's working through man he he he's a guy you always count on so I can't say enough good things about Jackson as a as a person and I appreciate what he brings to the game that toughness >> you've had 16 waiver claims as a team this year couple have been in your room with someone like Shaka or any of the waiver claims what do you say to them to keep them from being overwhelmed and their head spinning is there a plan which you give each one saying this is how much the playbook. I want you to know this week. >> He's exactly right. I think you approach it like any um anytime you're trying to onboard somebody, right? He's not going to know everything. You got to continue. You got to be patient, right? There'll be situations he's in. It may be the first time, but you're just constantly teaching. And I credit the the the room. I think the older linebackers do a great job of um pouring into him as well um to kind of get him caught up, which is very helpful. So, yeah, you you you don't give them everything. and you give them pieces of the puzzle and if there's something that comes up that we haven't had a chance to talk through then you coach it in the moment and uh you keep it moving you know that's the only approach you really can have cuz it's uh you when someone comes in and it's just uh you know it is what it is for >> on JB you reached 900 tackles last Sunday >> um eighth fastest player in the NFL to achieve that I asked this question to Shawn um he said obviously it's a ates that it just shows, you know, uh, his ability, right? But you also need the other 10 guys around you to be able to to achieve these types of things. But I'm just wondering how does it feed off from the, uh, to the rest of the unit, you know, to have a guy like that with those type of numbers. >> I think it's it's just excellence, but again, I echo what Sean and JB would say the same thing. I think, you know, in terms of a linebacker success, man, it's really tied to the front and I got roots as a front guy. So, I there is a there is definitely a collaborative uh impact that has to be that has to happen in order for Jordan to get that many tackles. He'd be the first to tell you that. But I think it's really cool. He again, he would never tell you that. Like I only reason I found out was because uh the media team put it out there, you know. So, he's he his head is down and he's he's uh you know, I think most important thing for him is winning and uh but it is cool. It is cool and I'm sure he feels proud of what he's done and and excited for what's ahead because I think he can continue to build on what he's done. >> What kind of question >> what kind of momentum have you seen with that relationship with the guys in the front and your guys on the second level as far as kind of understanding and >> reading their body and and anticipating when when they're going to try to put their head in a gap? How have you seen that come along thus far through the first seven games? >> I think it's progressed nicely. I think we're ask like so you think about the various fronts that you know uh defense plays, right? Um, I think being comfortable, um, number one with if you're a linebacker, being comfortable with what's in front of you and from the front end, being comfortable with kind of combinations that you could have. I think that always, you know, I think that helps you play faster. And so I think this is uh, you know, however however many games in you know like the more you do it, the better you get, the faster you play, the better you anticipate, right? And so that's really where I see the growth. And uh you know, we could we certainly are working to be better and better every week. We're going to be challenged this week, but um I think every week, every day we go out there, we get better. And uh we become tighter in that way.

title: Offensive Coordinator Bobby Slowik meets with the media | Miami Dolphins
text: So, correct me if I'm wrong. I think you went uptempo in one series. Have you done it, do you think, more than It was very briefly, just a couple plays where I don't know if it was a sugar huddle or what it was, but it was it was an uptempo approach for a couple of plays. It was mentioned on it might have been on the Jets broadcast, but what was it? I guess have you thought of doing it more or and if not, how much is just wanting to protect your defense terms of not having them on the field long? >> Yeah, I think it's always a given and take, right? like what we're trying to do from an offensive perspective. Obviously, we want to move the ball, but we also want to do things that we think are the best for the team. Now, the one thing I'll say about like going up tempo, um, is usually you do that when you think you can put your guys in a very predictable situation. Um, and the more predictable your tempo becomes, usually the less predictable situations we're putting them in. you know, like I just talking to my history, um I recall there's there's been a game I, you know, I went into as a coordinator like, man, this has been really good for us. We're going to live in this this game. That went bad real fast, you know, because all of a sudden you start getting different looks that you're not always planning for. Usually when you're going up tempo and on the ball, there's, you know, it's it's a smaller menu that you're choosing from. So, it's not like I'm bouncing around on you here, but you know, there there's a lot of reasons and thoughts for why you want to do it and when you want to do it. Um, and and I usually go to, okay, is this a time in the game or a moment in the game where I feel like if we go on the ball right now, we know what we're going to get and we're going to be able to take advantage of that in the run or the pass game. Um, and and really that kind of goes even to like twominut. A lot of people use twominute like it's very similar to a midgame on the ball situation, but it's really not. You know, like twominut are usually pretty specific offensive calls and pretty specific defensive calls and and it usually plays along the same lines. Like when it's predictable, everything's good and as soon as it starts getting unpredictable and you start getting unaccounted for situations, then then it it can from a scheme standpoint, it gets pretty hard. So, but long story short, it's always something we're talking about. It's always something we want up every game if we can. Um, can I use it more? Yeah. Can I use it less? Yeah. You know what I mean? Just depending on >> There's just no way of knowing if Malik would be better or your offense would be better playing uptempo if you don't use it. I guess you could judge it in practice, but is that something which you have a handle on? Would we be better if we played faster? >> Uh, yeah. We feel pretty good with with where we're at and how we play right now. And I I wouldn't really foresee that drastically changing, you know, as we keep going through the course of the season. >> And I'm sorry, I just have one final on the same issue. I know uh Logan Ryan on the CBS broadcast made a big deal about Malik and the offense taking a lot of time on the possession. I think at the eight or seven minute mark. Uh why was it done at that deliberate pace and not faster >> in which part of the game? You talking about going into half or in the fourth quarter? late, but prior to the uh to the Coleman touchdown that that trimmed the less >> late. I think, you know, it's it's one of those things. I I had to learn this as a play caller in the NFL. I'd been around Kyle doing it for a while, and I remember when I was with Kyle early on, like there were some times I was pay I was in the box. I'm just like, why aren't we going? Like, I'm freaking out. You know what I mean? Um that that's not that's usually not beneficial to you in the NFL. Like you you have an idea of where your threshold is in the fourth quarter of like, okay, we got to go and we got to go now. But I mean, I've been a part of a defensive NFL team where we gave up 21 points in like two minutes, you know? So, you you can catch lightning in a bottle fast, but as soon as you start going too fast and and you panic, it creates some issues. And with six minutes left in the game when you're only down 10 or 11, you know, like that, that's not panic time yet. That's time to make sure we go get points. That's really the biggest thing that I learned just from the people I've been with is when it gets down to crunch time and you're still talking a two-score game late in the game, like the most important thing that needs to happen is you need to get points. Uh, and I thought we did that. We started driving down the field. I mean, I think we got down into field goal range, something around fourish minutes left or something like that. And then we unfortunately we just didn't get the points. But, uh, that really was ultimately the goal. Bobby, how much attention do you pay to the yards before contact stat? >> Uh, I mean I to be perfectly honest with you, not not a lot. I mean, it was brought to my attention not but three weeks ago, you know what I mean? I didn't even know what it was. Um, I've look at it more now that I know what it is, you know, but it it doesn't a like a lot of what we see the stats just validate what you see. you know, you can spin stats in so many different ways depending on what kind of story you want to paint. You know, I mean, we kind of do it all the time as coaches. Um, when we're going into meetings, at the end of the day, all you're trying to really do is what's the tape say and what's that validate? And right right now, I would say it validates that that we're running the ball and blocking really well, you know, and then I would say the stats validate that. I think this last week was probably our first game. I thought, you know, there was more out there for us and we could have blocked better. Um, but by and large, you know, I'm I'm I'm there with a clicker in my hand. >> Bobby, you guys, um, speaking of stats, you have five receivers over 30 yards, nobody over 46, though. What does that tell you? Is that healthy? I mean, I'm sure you'd like to have a 100 yard receiver, but but is is that a healthy mix? >> Yeah, I mean, yeah, I always think it's good to spread the ball around. you know, anytime that you can really distribute the ball to a lot of different guys. I think that's a lot harder on the defense than when you have one guy that just all of a sudden is, you know, he goes for a hundred yards, they they usually then they know what they have to defend and take away, doesn't mean they can, but uh it it helps them just understand what it is they have to do where when you start distributing it and the quarterback's confident enough to to really get the ball distributed everywhere, uh that that gets really hard to stop really fast consistently. Um, and that that's the one thing for us we've been working on on offenses. We need to up our consistency. You know, I thought last game we had we had too many three and outs. Um, you know, which which it's it's a huge deal to me that we need to avoid. Uh, and a lot of that goes with consistency of execution, consistency of play calling, consistency of, you know, making sure we're doing the right thing in the pass game, distributing the ball to the right place, and our guys being in the right place. Um, so yeah, that that's really important to me. When we have a lot of targets to different people, it usually means we're we're getting across our progressions pretty good. >> It seemed like Malik was passing up some opportunities to run last game. What were you seeing in that regard? And why was that, if so? >> Yeah, you know, I think I think last week it it was a little easier to see some of them on film than I think it was live in the moment of the game. You know, the one thing I think that they do a really good job of is they mix up the rushes. They're a really good game team. They mix up how they game, where they game, and where the open windows are for you in the pass game. Uh, and it it can look like glaring sometimes when you're just watching strictly like to see if anyone can run. It's not as easy when you're looking at number one, number two, number three down the field to then recognize, oh man, I got a window, you know, and that that's something we're working on. We're we're training on and I know Malik's training on um but yeah, we we had some ops last week that we kind of left out there. We know that we're working towards making sure we take advantage of those. >> So, the Lions defense has been improving in points allowed per average. Like it was three weeks ago it was around 32 points per game. Now that dropped to 17.7. They just beat the last undefeated team in the NFL. So, what have you seen about their defense that they've been doing well and how um you know you can attack that basically? >> Yeah, I would say when you watch their film like the last three weeks has been really good football on defense. I think early in the year they had some games that got away from them. They they didn't uh play their best on defense like you know you could tell they just like what happens to everybody they had some mistakes or somebody just gives up a big play. You know it it was kind of a little bit of a roller coaster when you watch early in the year and I felt like uh Shep and Detroit's done a really good job the last three weeks kind of tightening up what they do uh really honing in on what they do and and they've gone out and they've played the last three weeks at a really high level and I mean they got a really good front. Um, I feel like I say that every week. I feel like every week we're playing a really good front, but you know, obviously they got Hutch. Uh, their two interior guys are really good. I mean, they're they're tough and they're playing towards that strength right now. So, it's it just like every week has been up to this, it's going to be a really good test for us. It's a really good test of, you know, our mentality, our physicality because that's how they play. When you speaking of their defense, their last and pass defense and maybe number four in sacks or something like that, what does that tell you about how the front works with the back? And does it tell you if we just give Malik Willis some time, he will have some [clears throat] hops? >> Yeah. Yeah, I was really interested in that. That that's one stat I did see early in the week and then I started watching the film and it didn't it didn't quite match what I thought I was going to see. You know, again, like early in the year, I think there were some there were some windows, there were some ops, there were some things people took advantage of and and really over the course of the season as the season's gone on, a lot of that is has shored up. Um, but you see an awful lot of teams playing from multiple scores behind, which usually going to up the pass uh percentage and the yards you gain and all all that stuff. So, like from what I see on tape, you know, like every week, I think we I think we got a a good scheme. I think we got a good approach. I think we got a good plan. I think our players are excited for this one. Uh but that's not to be confused with like this is going to be a tough one for us. We got to go out, we got to battle, and we're going to fight. >> How do you get the run game back on track Sunday? >> Uh yeah, it really just execution, you know, like I thought New England did a good job. Uh you know, with they they varied up a few looks. We kind of adjusted as we went through the game. Uh and and into the fourth quarter, we started to run the ball a little bit better there. Um, but you know, they they did a good job combined with us maybe not necessarily playing as well as we had up to up to this point last week. I didn't think in the run game we quite played with the conviction and like the aggression that we had in weeks before. So, this week's been a lot of talk about like, okay, let's get that back. What do we got to do scheme wise to still put you guys in good positions, but what do we got to do to get this attitude, this mentality back? And I think, you know, our guys are are 100% on board with that. And so far through uh two days of practice, you know, we're we're pleased with where we're at. >> From having to go a game without him, what was the impact of not having Kaden Proctor out there? >> Yeah, I mean, he just he's just a good player, you know what I mean? Like anytime you miss a good player, I think uh and he's not available in the game. It just obviously it limits a little bit of what you can do. I think King did a you know, it started off a little slow really for for everybody across the board. I thought we started slow, but King as the game went on, I thought he kind of fell into a rhythm. Um, and he started playing better, especially, you know, in in the second half. I thought he really kind of honed into what he needed to do by and large. Um, but, you know, still when when Proc's out there, you can feel Proctor's presence on most every play. You know, he's just a massive guy who can move. He displaces people. He's putting defensive tackles five, six yards down the field. He caps off at the end of plays. We throw the ball 10 yards down the field for a 30 yard explosive and next thing you know Proctor's showing up in the screen. Everyone's like, "Where'd he come from?" You know what I mean? So, he just he just gives everybody a lot of energy when he's out there and then that's that's not even including uh what you can do with him scheme wise. >> You guys matched up against the Lions during joint practices last year. What do you remember about that experience that will help you on Sunday? >> Yeah, I mean, we had two practices against them then, you know, and and I think it's interesting when you think back to it. And I'm sure they're kind of thinking the same. Like our offense is different and evolved a little bit. Their defense has evolved quite a bit from what it was in those joint practices. You know, you go through a full season and then the beginning of a second season, it's natural that like the the little wrinkles that you have kind of they all change. Some of that's personnel dependent. Some of that maybe is is uh scheme dependent by them. Um, but I I thought it was good for us and will be good for us again to play just that that style of of um I guess you can say attitude, you know, like demeanor that they play with, tone that they play with because it's it's the same way we want to play and we believe in playing. Um, just like last week, you know, I thought last week we played a team that believes in playing the way we do, it'll be the same this week. And I think anytime you're able to go against that, it's the old saying, iron sharpens iron. You know what I mean? So you come out of that better than you went into it. >> With regard to the uh to the INT, the bounced up Daquan Jones helmet. Uh what comment from Willis afterward is that there's really nothing he could do about that. In general, I wouldn't ask you to review every pass that he's had that's been knocked down. But in general, is there anything that he could be doing better to try to eliminate off a body part of someone or being deflected by defensive linemen? Yeah, that one was a little unusual because he he got hit right in the back around the arm area right when he was letting it go, which, you know, can affect more than you think it can. That being said, uh, a coach is always going to find something. You know, you're always going to just pick apart and find something to be like, maybe you could have, I think we should have, you know, so we have those conversations like all the time. Um, it's something, you know, he he knows nobody wants to have a ball ricochet off a defensive tackle and then wind up as an interception. I mean, that that stinks for the quarterback. So, I mean, he's he's been doing a great job of just being willing to take whatever he can get, try to incorporate it into what [clears throat] we do and and keep working on it, keep grinding on it, see if it we can get it to show up on Sundays. Um, and then there's some that that are fluke situations that you can't quite handle and you just got to be willing to say that's out of my control and I can only control what I can control and let me go out and let me rip the next one. >> You guys have faced a lot of good pass rushers. What are some of the things you want to be mindful of uh game plan against Aiden Hutchinson? >> Yeah, I think I think it'd probably be easier for us if it wasn't just Aiden. Uh, you know, but you know, McNeel's one of the better interior rushers we're going to play this year. Um, they got 91's a really good player. So, it's more than just him, but specifically as it pertains to the edge. Uh, you know, we're going to have to make sure in protection that we're doing a good job helping. Might not always be with a chip or a crack, but you know, you can help with slides, you can help with different ways of influencing the guys. So, but a large part of what we're doing, we're making sure that somehow someway our tackles feel like they're not on islands, you know, all day every day. And then on top of that, you balance that out with scheme. like eventually you're going to have to block the guy one-on-one, but can we get rid of the ball fast? Can we have some screens that offset it? Can we do some runs that offset it? Uh, which I think we've done a good job of through the course of the year in passing situation. We've hit some runs that have slowed down some rushes. So, it's really just continuing to change it up and when you have to go back and you got to see it, you got to throw, we got to make sure that we're helping our tackles out. >> Last question, >> Bobby. Is Kron Allen close to being able to contribute from scrimmage? We saw he had a couple of nice plays on special teams last week, but where is he as far as contributing from scrimmage? >> Yeah, he's he's progressing, you know. Uh it's been cool to see him in practice every week, get a little more comfortable with what we do and and watch him. I mean, he works his tail off when he gets a chance on scout team and when he's with us. I thought it was really awesome to see him on special teams last week, make two big plays. title: Mike Evans, 49ers WR Trade UPDATE...
text: Our first major post by update from John Lynch. Likely no Mike Evans, likely no Debo Samuel this week against the Raiders for the 49ers. And we had read in between the lines of the past couple of days to surmise that and John Lynch said on KNBR that it is unlikely that the 49ers see both of those veteran wide receivers. However, they are in better shape at the wide receiver position for this game already because DeMarcus Robinson is on track to be back and they do have Kadarius Hodge back on the team. That helps the 49ers a lot on special teams at gunner. Plus it's going to be Christian Kirk's second game with the San Francisco, so maybe we can expect them to be a little bit more involved with the offense. That being said, still a lot of receivers down including Evans, including Debo Samuel, De'Shawn Shrubling, all of whom the 49ers expect to return, but there's so much talk about a potential trade, especially since the 49ers did have the framework of a trade for Jauan Jennings set up with Minnesota. More on that in a bit. First, let's listen into John Lynch talking about the potential of a wide receiver trade, obviously outside of Jauan Jennings. >> We will see, you know, we have till Tuesday at 1:00 out here after the Raiders game, so um the the trade deadline's jumping on us. Um you know, we're excited to get a couple guys back. DeMarcus Robinson uh back out on the field yesterday and uh you know, looked to come out of that pretty well. We got to get him through today's practice. Thursday's kind of a grind of a practice, so can he handle that volume? D-Rob was really on a good path, so having him back is a is a really good sign for us. Kadarius Hodge came back, joined our practice squad. Kadarius was playing some good football. And in the coming weeks, you know, we uh hope to get Deebo and and Mike back in the fold as well. So, we've got those guys coming back. Um as I've said consistently, you know, we've we've we probably made the move that we were most targeted on in the Deebo move and and that may be it and we're really happy with our team. But, we'll see, you know, we'll keep keep the phones working until Tuesday at 12:58, I guess, and and uh see see what what else we can do or that may be it and if so, we we really we we love this team. >> I see consistent theme from social media every single year and it's this mentality that it's like Madden. It's like a video game that you could just press a button and a trade will happen. And it really does not work that way. The 49ers and John Lynch have perhaps the most impressive track record, the most robust track record of making value trades. Like and I'm talking about splash and value. I've made the Venn diagram. I've showed that to you before. We can pull it up later in the show, but the amount of value splash trades, the ones that overlap there in that middle sliver of the Venn diagram that the 49ers have made over the course of the past 10 years has been second to none in the NFL. So, they trade as prolifically and effectively as anybody in the league. And I would say that they're at the very top. You cannot just wish that the 49ers will get Garrett Wilson. Press a button and have it happen. It doesn't work that way. Why? Because several factors have to align for that to actually come to fruition. The most important of which is that the Jets actually have to be willing to trade Garrett Wilson. So, as much fan fantasy as there is about every single one of these trades, you have to realize that they're not realistic until they they actually like have the ingredients to happen and for that the stars do have to align. So, of course the 49ers are going to be working the phones. Of course they're going to be doing their best to try to make something that makes sense happen, but I will say that at a certain point you need your own guys that you began the season with to be reasonably healthy in order for your team to have the best chance to make a run at the Super Bowl. Otherwise like health wouldn't matter at all in this league and you could just hit a button every single time that a guy got hurt and you could replace them effectively with a trade and it is not that simple. So, that's where John Lynch is coming from. The 49ers have already made one massive splash this trade season. That was for DeForest Buckner. They're not done. They're still trying to work the phones and do what they can to get somebody else in there and obviously we look at wide receiver as a potential position of need, but they do in fact have a lot of guys coming back at that position. Now, the one trade that they had agreed to in principle with the Minnesota Vikings for a wide receiver was for Jauan Jennings, but that fell through after the 49ers talked to Jauan Jennings. However, it does give us clues about how the 49ers are looking at this wide receiver position and looking at the trade deadline and I thought that John Lynch divulged and really confirmed one very, very important piece of the Jauan Jennings puzzle when he spoke on KNBR. >> I have an interesting situation where um you know, we were a little banged up at at receiver. You know, you hear things. Uh you watch film and and you know, I think it's no secret Jauan hasn't been targeted a whole lot in Minnesota. Um you know, for multiple reasons and we just inquired and and Nolan Tiesley came from Seattle. I didn't know Nolan that well, but really have come to enjoy him um through that process and you know, it was a situation like they didn't you know, you they didn't they basically knew that Jauan uh wasn't happy with the amount of targets he was getting, but he seemed to kind of enjoy it said, "Look, we we want to uh try to put Jauan in the best situation. Let's work the framework of a deal." But, I said during the whole time, "Look, we're going to have to talk with Jauan. We've had a history with him. We love him to death. Um, but we got to let him know exactly kind of what his role will be, uh what our expectations are." And And so, we did that and I I thought we had a framework of a deal. We talked to Jauan. I talked to him first and brought the phone down to Kyle. We got on a FaceTime with him and Kyle did a great job saying, "Jauan, here's what it will be now. Here's what it will be in the future. We'd love to have you, but you got a decision to make and and you know, Jauan ended up um you know, calling back along with Nolan and saying, "Hey, he's he's decided to stay here." So, I don't want to make any more. That's the honest-to-god's truth of what happened and and Jauan made a decision. You know, there's a lot that goes into these things like dawned upon me when DeForest comes here. He's got three kids. You're talking kids in school. You're talking houses that you're leaving and new houses you have to find. So, there's a When I say there's multiple layers to these things, um you know, they're all multiple layers and I I was actually proud of the way we worked with Minnesota to try to see what really what was Obviously, everybody's got your team's best interest, but also, hey, there's a player involved here. Let's try to do right by him. Uh you know, we made a a play at it and and Jauan made a decision that he you know, ultimately, he was happy there and and uh you know, we moved on. >> So, John Lynch said out loud what Kyle Shanahan didn't quite say out loud yesterday and that's that they talked about Jauan Jennings' role on the FaceTime conversation. And I think that it's not too hard to read in between the lines. The 49ers looking at their wide receiver room now, looking at it what it had been before the injuries and looking at what it's projected to be once all these guys do return from injury, they likely offer Juwan Jennings a limited role. That was part of the discussion, part of the many layers that John Lynch talked about. There are several other facets to this that we can surmise were discussed or at least considered by Juwan Jennings when he was making his decision, including the cost of living in California. You could talk about state income tax as well. I mean, all of this is part of a layered discussion, right? This is a job. This is a business. These are the professions of these men. This is the livelihood of these men. But when it comes to the actual role on the field for the 49ers, it's a tricky situation at the wide receiver room because they are in this valley right now, right? The valley of health. They had a peak of health, it's dipped into a valley, but it's going to come back out on the other side and they should be much healthier and much more available moving forward. So, what they're looking at right now is a way to bridge the gap between now and when they get healthier. That's probably going to be the most possible potential acquisition. Somebody who bridges the gap, somebody who can pick up the playbook quickly so you don't have to spend a month teaching him the ins and outs of what they're running and by the time he learns it, well, the Mike Evans and everybody is back. So, Juwan Jennings, I think really fit into that mold perfectly. Obviously he's been in the system before, could be somebody who's uh fits right now, doesn't have to learn the Kyle Shanahan playbook and uh would be able to help out in the time being, but probably would see his role diminished after everybody returned. Especially De'Shawn Shribling way down the road. And I think the 49ers were up front with Juwan Jennings about that. I think that Kyle Shanahan and John Lynch said, "Hey, we know it's more expensive to live in California, so we we want to really make sure that you would be happy here because we don't want anybody who's unhappy on this football team." They don't want to mess up the locker room chemistry and they know that Juwan's a warrior, they know that he's going to take a lot of stuff personally and in a good way, in a way that's really helped the 49ers before, but they told him straight up, "If if this role, which could diminish over time with these guys coming back, uh doesn't fit you, if you think you'd be happier in Minnesota, just tell us and we won't make the trade. We're going to do right by you. We have a good relationship with you and we're not going to force you to come to a place, even though he didn't have a no-trade clause, we're not going to force you to come to a place that you don't want to be." And Juwan thought about it, called John and Kyle back and said, "You know, I I'd rather be here in Minnesota." He balanced all of the factors and that was that. That means the 49ers continue to be on the lookout for value at the wide receiver position. Can it potentially come through a massive splash? Of course, it can. Will it likely come through a massive splash? No. But say that the Jets do end up deciding that they'd trade Garrett Wilson. "We really want to get rid of Garrett Wilson and there's a good price for Garrett Wilson out there, one that the 49ers can stomach." You look at the potential long-term value of a move like that and it is immense because you don't know how much longer Mike Evans is going to play. You want it to make Brandon Aiyuk your long-term X wide receiver, but that didn't work out. We'll see how that all materializes, by the way, over the next couple days. Aiyuk has said through his agent, Drew Rosenhaus, that he plans to show up on Friday, but everything on that front remains TBD. It's an unprecedented situation. John Lynch even said, "We have no playbook for this." So, we'll see how it goes over the next couple days, but obviously, Aiyuk didn't work out. Evans was meant to be a short-term band-aid. He's a very good Hall of Fame band-aid at that, but as you can see, he's out with the Achilles issue right now. We'll see when he's back and then we'll see about future seasons. I mean, Brock Purdy and company could really benefit from having a stable fixture X wide receiver for several seasons. So, perhaps there is value to be found in a big splash X wide receiver for but that doesn't mean that there's an X-wide receiver pick-up to be found on the market. Stuff has to align, and a lot of that is often out of your control. Everything aligned in 2022 when the 49ers traded for Christian McCaffrey. Much less had to align for them to trade for DeForest Buckner, but still you had to have some things out of your control work in your favor such as the Colts not being good and willing to sell this year. So, then you could talk about other receiver names like Josh Downs of Indianapolis, and then you wonder, well, does that align with what you're trying to do with Brock Purdy? Do you want a taller weapon? That's more of a 5-9 shorter guy, but he could also return punts. I've talked about uh I Xavier Hutchinson. I don't know if the Texans uh want to sell him though. That's that's TBD. He's a taller 6-3 receiver who's worked with Purdy before at Iowa State and and on the final season of his contract. So, we can discuss all these possibilities, but that doesn't mean that the 49ers can just press a button and make them happen. So much else has to materialize for those possibilities to actually become reality, which is why the only viable strategy is the one that John Lynch outlines. Like, you you have to sit back and put the ball around the hoop as as often and as much as possible, and every once in a while it's going to go through the hoop. It did for DeForest Buckner, and now we'll see if it does moving forward for any other 49ers acquisitions. Remember that when they traded Buckner away back in 2020, that was just a few weeks before they traded for Trent Williams. You could talk about the stars aligning getting Trent Williams for what? A three and a five from Washington in 2020, and now he's become this fixture at tackle for over half a decade for the 49ers. Uh that that was an example of a splash value trade for the 49ers. I think they got another splash value trade with DeForest Buckner, and we'll see what they're able to get moving forward. Obviously, John Lynch thinks they got splash and value with Buckner and I thought that he had some really, really interesting quotes about the Forest Buckner in this trade on KNBR. >> Obviously, he's uh DeForest has had a tremendous career. The faithful are are very familiar with him. Um you know, and we we ran into a situation 6 years ago where we were you know, we were doing some salary cap forecast and trying to best best ascertain and we we got a call from Chris Ballard and the Colts.
